item.description:
The front page gains the Federation tab: a card for every system that has Spire on it.

Added

  • **Federation surface**: the main window now switches between Apps, Endpoints, and Federation. The Federation page shows a card per machine — This Mac's card carries its identity, version, endpoint, Place a Model, and what's placed; every fleet machine's card shows live reachability, its installed Spire build, and the roles its endpoint reports, checked over the same trusted channel the fleet updater uses.
  • The machine list is data: Federation/machines.json in Spire's data folder, seeded with the fleet and editable. Paired machines will feed these same cards when pairing ships.

Changed

  • Placing a model no longer requires the Settings window — the same form lives on the Federation page's This Mac card (Settings keeps it too; both are one implementation).

Installing Spire now brings its core organ with it: Apple's container tool arrives as part of Spire, never as an errand.

Added

  • **The container tool installs itself**: when first-run setup finds Apple's container tool missing, Spire downloads Apple's own signed installer (pinned version, checksum-verified, signature-verified as Apple's Containerization team, notarization-checked) and opens it in the macOS Installer. Your only touch is the standard install flow; Spire notices when the tool arrives, starts the container system, and re-checks. A retry button appears only if something failed.
  • **Fleet installs carry the tool**: the fleet update lane now ensures the container tool on every Studio on every pass — installed over SSH with macOS's own installer when absent — and caches the verified package on the NAS so installs stay on the local network.

Changed

  • The tool is used exactly as Apple built it — Spire's entire authorship is a one-line version pin; Apple maintains everything inside the tool.

The front page grows a second surface: administering your endpoints is now as first-class as administering your apps.

Added

  • **Endpoints surface**: the main window switches between Apps and Endpoints. The Endpoints page lists servers in a sidebar (this Mac today; federated Macs join as the federation lands) with status, Start/Stop/Restart, the endpoint URL displayed and copyable, and a card for each serving role.
  • **Live link acknowledgement**: the Hugging Face model link answers as you type — what was recognized, or exactly what's wrong — before any download.
  • **Token verification**: the Hugging Face access token proves itself the moment it's entered ("signed in as ⟨name⟩", rejected, or unreachable) and is saved on verification. It's entered once, not per download.
  • **Living download meter**: the progress bar fills while the percentage visibly counts beside it.
  • **Error console**: failures present in plain language with Dismiss and View Log always offered, and an Auto-Fix button when the remedy is documented — the first: an incomplete download offers "Download Again."
  • **Federation tab** in Settings: this Mac's pairing identity, moved out of Advanced, ready for the one-time pairing ceremony.

Changed

  • Settings reorganized to one tab per concern: Models, Federation, Advanced.
  • The app-level test suite runs again (a build setting had silenced it since it was created); node identity code adopted into the app package properly.
